content.text: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod. My name is Marco.
content.trans: 你好，大家欢迎来到英语广播。我的名字是Marco。

content.text: And my name is Catherine and today we're talking about a very important day in a couple's life.
content.trans: 而且我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们要谈论的是这对夫妇生活中非常重要的一天。

content.text: That's right. We're going to a wedding. But this time it's not going to be so romantic because actually the groom is having second thoughts about the wedding.
content.trans: 那就是了。我们去的是婚礼。但是这次可不浪漫了，因为其实新郎对婚礼有点犹豫了。

content.text: Okay. That means he's nervous and he's not positive. He wants to get married today.
content.trans: 好的。这意味着他很紧张，也不确定。他今天想要结婚。

content.text: So remember the groom is the man. The bride is the woman. Let's jump right into this dialogue.
content.trans: 所以记住，新郎是男人。新娘是女人。让我们直接进入这段对话。

content.text: Listen to what's going on and when we come back we'll be talking about some of the words and phrases you've heard.
content.trans: 听一听发生了什么，我们下次回来时会谈谈你听到的一些单词和短语。

content.text: Man, I'm freaking out. You gotta help me.
content.trans: 人类，我好慌。你得帮我。

content.text: Whoa, whoa, take it easy. Relax.
content.trans: 哇，哇，放松点。

content.text: Tease, you're sweating like a pig. What's going on?
content.trans: 你汗流浃背像个猪一样。怎么了？

content.text: I can't go through with this. I just can't. I'm not ready for marriage. What was I thinking? I'm only 35 years old.
content.trans: 我不能继续下去了。我真的做不到。我还没有准备好结婚。我当时是怎么想的？我才35岁。

content.text: I've got my entire life ahead of me. Adventure's waiting. I can't settle down yet. What are you talking about?
content.trans: 我已经拥有了一生的冒险。探险等着我。我还未安定下来。你在说什么？

content.text: It wasn't more than a month ago that you were rambling on about how you are tired of living the life of a bachelor and how you envy your friends that have a family.
content.trans: 不就是上个月的事吗，你还在说不想过单身生活，羡慕那些有家人的朋友。

content.text: I know. I know. Let's think this through.
content.trans: 我知道。我知道。我们好好想想吧。

content.text: First of all, you cannot leave Amy at the altar. Not only will she be humiliated and kill you, but she is the woman that you love and the woman of your dreams.
content.trans: 首先，你绝不能把艾米留在神坛上。她不仅会受到羞辱并杀死你，而且她是你的爱人和心中所梦的女子。

content.text: Why would you want to end that or jeopardize it like this?
content.trans: 为什么你要这样结束它，甚至危及其存在？

content.text: Second of all, you were just getting cold feet. You know, deep down inside that you want to marry her. So cut the crap and do it.
content.trans: 其次，你只是在打退堂鼓。你知道，骨子里你想娶她。所以别扯淡了，赶紧做吧。

content.text: You're right. I'm being crazy. Okay, I'm ready. Let's do this.
content.trans: 你是对的。我发疯了。好的，我已经准备好了。让我们开始吧。

content.text: Great. That was a close one. You had me going there for a minute. I thought I was going to have to slap some sense into you.
content.trans: 很好。那可是差点儿把我逼急了。我以为我得用拳头教训你呢。

content.text: All right, we're back. So almost. He almost didn't get married, but luckily you have a good friend to help you out.
content.trans: 好的，我们又回来了。差不多了。幸好你有一个好朋友帮你解决了问题。

content.text: Exactly. So this friend really saved the day, made sure that the groom didn't get too nervous and had some really positive words.
content.trans: 确实。这个朋友真是救了大家的忙，确保新郎不会过于紧张，并且说了些非常积极的话。

content.text: So let's take a listen to some of these marriage words in today's language takeaway.
content.trans: 那么，让我们听听今天的语言快餐中的一些婚姻词汇。

content.text: Language takeaway. All right. So as you mentioned, we have this word marriage. Now marriage is the noun form, right, of actually getting married or to be married.
content.trans: 语言取巧。好的。正如您所提到的，我们有这个词“婚姻”，而婚姻是“结婚”这个动词的名词形式，即实际上结婚或被结婚。

content.text: Right. Marriage is the noun, the word that describes the relationship between two married people. Okay. And so you have a relationship, maybe you're dating, but once you get married,
content.trans: 好的。婚姻是名词，指的是两个已婚人士之间的关系。好吧。所以你有关系，也许你在约会，但一旦结婚，

content.text: the thing between you as a man and a woman, that's your marriage. Your marriage. You could say our marriage is in danger.
content.trans: 作为男人和女人之间的那件事，那就是你的婚姻。你的婚姻。你可以这么说，我们的婚姻处于危险之中。

content.text: We need to work on our marriage. Exactly. Or we have a happy marriage. All right. Okay. So that's marriage. Now if you get married, and this guy he mentioned a phrase which was to settle down.
content.trans: 我们需要好好工作。或者我们有一个幸福的婚姻。好的。这就是婚姻了。现在如果你结婚，他提到过要安定下来。

content.text: To settle down. This is a very important phrase. To settle down means to get serious, mature, and to stop living like a child.
content.trans: 安顿下来。这是一个非常重要的话。安顿下来意味着要认真、成熟，并停止像孩子一样生活。

content.text: It means really to have a house or to start having kids. It's a time and life. So to settle down is to become more stable, right.
content.trans: 这其实是要有一个房子，或者开始有孩子。这是一个时间和生活的问题。所以安定下来就是更稳定了。

content.text: As you say, to buy a house, to have a family, to stay in one place and not be so adventurous or stuff like that. Exactly. So it's to calm down and to be more fixed in life.
content.trans: 正如你说的那样，为了买房子、生孩子、呆在一个地方而不那么冒险。完全正确。所以是为了平静下来，更加固定在生活上。

content.text: All right. Now the opposite of this would be to be a bachelor. Right. So bachelor is a single man, someone who's not married.
content.trans: 好的。这的反义词就是单身汉。对了，单身汉是指未婚的男人。

content.text: And you often hear this term when we talk about apartments. So bachelor pad is an apartment that's specific to a single man.
content.trans: 而且当我们谈论公寓时，经常会听到这个词。所以“单身宿舍”是指专属于单个男人的公寓。

content.text: Usually there's lots of video games and a fancy TV and a pool table. Exactly. All right. So bachelor, we had a lesson about this called bachelor party.
content.trans: 通常会有许多视频游戏，一台高档电视和一张台球桌。没错。好的。所以单身汉，我们上了一堂关于这个的课程，叫做“单身汉派对”。

content.text: Right. Which is a party for a man right before he gets married. Okay. And bachelor is a special word for a man who's not married.
content.trans: 好的。这是即将结婚前的男子聚会。对了，单身是未婚男性的特殊称呼。

content.text: Okay. Very good. And now as they were talking about not getting married, he said that you can't leave Amy at the altar.
content.trans: 好的。很好。现在他们正在谈论不结婚时，他说你不能把艾米留在圣坛上。

content.text: So you often hear this in movies. She got left at the altar or you can't leave her at the altar. This word altar is actually religious.
content.trans: 所以你经常在电影中听到这个。她被留在了圣坛或者你不能把心爱的人留在圣坛。这个词“圣坛”实际上是指宗教。

content.text: This altar is the table in a church where the priest does all of his work. Right. Right. So an altar is a special religious table.
content.trans: 这个祭坛就是教堂里主教做所有工作的桌子。对，对。所以，祭坛是一个特殊的宗教桌子。

content.text: So usually two people will stand in front of an altar and get married, right, with the priest who is doing his thing there.
content.trans: 所以通常两个人会在祭坛前结婚，对吧，那里有一个正在做自己事情的牧师。

content.text: Exactly. He says, do you joke, take Samantha to be your bride blah blah blah. So that happens at a special place called the altar. Okay. Very good.
content.trans: 的确。他说，你开个玩笑吧，把萨曼莎嫁给你的废话一堆。所以发生在神圣的地方叫圣台。好的。很好。

content.text: It's also common in the normal mass like on Sundays. Right. Okay. And for the last word or phrase today, it's to get cold feet.
content.trans: 这也是正常情况下常见的，比如在周日。对了。今天要说的最后一个词或短语是“打退堂鼓”。

content.text: You're just getting cold feet. Okay. So this is a very funny phrase in English because it doesn't actually mean that your your your your cold feet are cold. Right.
content.trans: 你只是在打退堂鼓。好吧。这个英文中的短语非常有趣，因为它实际上并不是说你的脚真的变冷了。

content.text: So cold feet means you're nervous about something. You you might change your mind. Okay. Okay. So people often talk about men and women getting cold feet before a wedding.
content.trans: 所以，冷场意味着你对某件事感到紧张。你可能会改变主意。好的。好的。人们常常谈论在婚礼前男人和女人会变得冷场。

content.text: But you can also relate it to any other situation, not only getting married, right. Yeah. For example, I'm going to go jump out of an airplane tomorrow. Okay.
content.trans: 但是，你也可以把它和其他任何情况联系起来，不仅仅是结婚。是的。例如，我明天要从飞机上跳下去。好吧。

content.text: Fast forward tomorrow. Oh no. I have cold feet. I don't think I want to jump out of an airplane. Okay. So that's the good cold feet to have second thoughts or doubts about actually doing something.
content.trans: 快进明天。啊，不好。我脚冰凉。我不想跳飞机。行。这就是做第二回决定或怀疑自己是否真的要做某事的好的脚气。

content.text: Exactly. Cold feet. All right. So why don't we listen to our dialogue again? Let's keep a look out for all of these words and we'll be back in a little bit.
content.trans: 确实。害羞。好吧。让我们再听听我们的对话吧？我们会在这些词上保持警惕，一会儿就回来。

content.text: Man, I'm freaking out. You got to help me. Whoa. Whoa. Take it easy. Relax. Cheese. You're sweating like a pig. What's going on? I can't go through with this. I just can't. I'm not ready for marriage. What was I thinking? I'm only 35 years old.
content.trans: 男人，我好慌。你得帮我啊。哇。哇。冷静点。放松。奶酪。你汗流浃背的像个猪一样。发生了什么事？我不能继续下去了。我真的做不到。我还没准备好结婚。我当时是怎么想的？我才35岁。

content.text: I've got my entire life ahead of me. Adventure's waiting. I can't settle down yet. What are you talking about?
content.trans: 我已经拥有了一生的冒险。等待着我的是新的开始。我还没准备好安定下来。你在说什么？

content.text: It wasn't more than a month ago that you were rambling on about how you are tired of living the life of a bachelor and how you envy your friends that have a family.
content.trans: 那才不过上个月的事，你就一直在说你厌倦了单身生活，并且羡慕那些有家人的朋友。

content.text: I know. I know. Let's think this through. First of all, you cannot leave Amy at the altar. Not only will she be humiliated and kill you, but she is the woman that you love and the woman of your dreams.
content.trans: 我知道。我知道。我们得好好想想。首先，你不能把艾米丢在人情债上。她不仅会受辱，还会杀掉你，而且她是你的爱人和心中的女神。

content.text: Why would you want to end that or jeopardize it like this? Second of all, you were just getting cold feet. You know, deep down inside that you want to marry her.
content.trans: 为什么你要这样结束它呢？第二，你只是在打退堂鼓。你知道，从内心深处来说，你想嫁给她。

content.text: So cut the crap and do it. You're right. I'm being crazy. Okay. I'm ready. Let's do this. Great.

content.text: Whew. That was a close one. You had me going there for a minute. I thought I was going to have to slap some sense into you.

content.text: All right. We're back. So now why don't we take a look at four key phrases that we found in this dialogue on Fluency Builder.

content.text: Fluency Builder.
content.trans: 流利 builder.

content.text: This first one is a really great phrase because it's very, well, it's easy to picture this what we're describing. Sweating like a pig.
content.trans: 这个短语真的很棒，因为它很容易让人想象我们正在描述的内容。汗如猪流。

content.text: To sweat like a pig. Okay. You're sweating like a pig. All right. This is a way to say that someone is sweating a lot.
content.trans: 流汗如猪。好吧。你汗流浃背了。好了。这是一句表示某人出汗很多的话。

content.text: A lot. Okay. And it's really gross or disgusting. No, do pigs actually sweat?
content.trans: 很多。好的。这真的很难闻或恶心。不，猪实际上出汗吗？

content.text: I don't know if pigs actually sweat, but you imagine someone smells bad and they have, you know, sweat on their face and their back and their arms.
content.trans: 我不清楚猪是否真的出汗，但我认为如果你想象一个人闻到难闻的气味，并且他们脸上、后背和手臂上都有汗液，那么他们确实可能在出汗。

content.text: All right. Well, sometimes don't you say you're sweating like a dog? You could also say that. I guess we like animals in English, but this is just a really great way to say that someone is really sweating.
content.trans: 好的。嗯，你不是说汗流浃背吗？你也可以说成是这样。我想我们喜欢动物吧，在英语里，这真是一个非常棒的方式来表达某人真的在出汗。

content.text: All right. And while he was sweating and he was really nervous because he said, I can't go through with this. What does he mean go through with this? With what?
content.trans: 好的。他汗流浃背，非常紧张，因为他说道：“我不能完成这个。” 这个“完成”指的是什么？

content.text: To go through with means to actually do something. Okay. So maybe I say, I don't want to jump out of an airplane. I can't go through with this. Okay. I can't jump.
content.trans: 继续意味着实际上去做某事。好的。也许我会说，我不想从飞机上跳出来。我不能完成这个任务。好的。我不可以跳。

content.text: So it depends on what we're actually talking about. Okay. If we're talking about a wedding, you say I can't go through with this. I can't get married.
content.trans: 所以这取决于我们说的是什么。好吧。如果你说我们要举行婚礼，你可以说我不能进行下去了，我不能结婚。

content.text: So if you're planning a robbery, you say, well, in the last minute, I couldn't go through with it. I backed out. I can't complete what I talked about doing. Okay.
content.trans: 所以如果你计划盗窃，你可以说：“好吧，在最后一刻，我没能完成它。我退缩了。我不能完成我说要做的事情。”

content.text: And now the friend, he finally gets kind of angry and he says, cut the crap. Oh, man, this is a very common phrase. All right. This is, this is someone says this if they don't want to listen to complain anymore. Okay.
content.trans: 现在这个朋友，他终于有点生气了，他说：“别废话。”哦，天啊，这真是一个非常常见的短语。好吧，如果某人不想再听抱怨了的话。

content.text: Marco, cut the crap. Okay. I don't want to hear your excuses. I don't want to hear your complaints. I want to just hear solutions.
content.trans: 马可，滚开。好吧，我不想听你的借口。我不想听你的抱怨。我想听听解决方案。

content.text: Solutions, ideas, positive things. So to cut the crap is no more complaints, no more excuses, or no more talking nonsense.
content.trans: 解决方案、想法、积极的事情。所以，甩开废话就是没有抱怨、没有借口、也没有胡说八道。

content.text: Exactly. And this is, this is common among teachers and well, parents. All right. So cut the crap. Now it's not very polite, right? So you wouldn't really say it to your boss or like a friend.
content.trans: 确实。这在老师和家长中很常见，对吧？好吧，现在听起来不太礼貌了，是吗？所以你不会真的对你的老板或朋友说的。

content.text: Cut the crap is kind of rude and it's very spoken language. So I would write it down and I would not use this with someone who is like a teacher. Well, yeah, like an authority.
content.trans: 直话直书有点儿粗鲁，是口语中常见的表达方式。所以我会写下它，并且不会在像老师这样的人面前使用。对了，就像权威人士一样。

content.text: You don't use it with them. They might use it with you. Okay. And for our last phrase, he said, whoo, you had me going there for a while or you had me going there for a minute.
content.trans: 你用它时他们不会。他们会用它来你。好吧。最后的短语他说，哇，我差点以为是你要我去那里了，或者我以为是你去那里的时间很短。

content.text: Okay. So this is a really interesting phrase. We use this a lot in English, but it's not clear from listening to it, what it might mean. So you had me going there. In this sense means, oh, I was really nervous for a minute.
content.trans: 好的。所以这是一个非常有趣的短语。我们在英语中经常使用它，但听上去并不清楚这个短语可能意味着什么。因此你让我有点困惑了。在这个意义上，我真的很紧张了一分钟。

content.text: I really believed what you were saying.
content.trans: 我真的相信你说的话。

content.text: Exactly. So maybe we could give an example, Marco. All right.
content.trans: 确实。所以也许我们可以举个例子，马可。好的。

content.text: Did you know that yesterday I won a lottery. I mean, I won like a million dollars and I had the perfect numbers.
content.trans: 你知道吗，昨天我中了彩票。我意思是，我中了一百万美元，我有完美的号码。

content.text: Oh, my God. Really? Can I have a million dollars?
content.trans: 哦，我的天啊。真的吗？我能有百万美元吗？

content.text: You had me going there for a minute. You actually believe me. You believe me. Okay, maybe not. He's not that goal.

content.text: That goal. All right. But that that's what it means, right?
content.trans: 那个目标。好的。但那不就是它的意思吗？

content.text: To believe someone's story or to think that something's going to happen even though it doesn't. Right.
content.trans: 相信某人的故事或认为事情会发生的，尽管它并没有发生。没错。

content.text: You had me going there. That means what you thought was going to happen didn't happen.
content.trans: 你让我以为那是会发生的事情没发生。

content.text: So you can use it in the third person is like, yeah, I was telling him this awesome story and I really had him going for a while.
content.trans: 所以你可以用第三人称来使用它，就像我告诉他是这个棒极了的故事，而且真的让他很着迷了好一会儿。

content.text: He really believed me. And then I told him it wasn't true. Okay.

content.text: What are you talking about? It wasn't more than a month ago that you were rambling on about how you are tired of living the life of a bachelor and how you envy your friends that have a family.

content.text: I thought I was going to have to slap some sense into you.
content.trans: 我以为我必须用拳头教训你。

content.text: Alright, so this is a popular scenario, right? Somebody at the moment on their wedding day, they get cold feet and they, you know, they back out.
content.trans: 好的，所以这种情况很常见吧？某人在婚礼当天突然后悔了，他们就这样反悔了。

content.text: TV, movies, books, everyone loves this situation. Have you ever actually heard of or experienced or maybe known of somebody who actually left the bride at the altar or the groom at the altar?
content.trans: 电视、电影、书籍，大家都喜欢这种状况。你有没有真正听说过或亲身经历过或者可能知道有人真的在新郎新娘都到不了教堂时就离开了？

content.text: I don't know anyone who did that luckily. I think it's really sad. I mean, you know, I don't think it's really that common.
content.trans: 我也不知道谁干的这么幸运。我觉得真让人难过。我知道，你不知道，这事儿真的很普遍。

content.text: Now, but there was a movie just about this. So there's a woman, Julia Roberts, who tries and tries and tries to get married but never can.
content.trans: 现在，但有一部关于这件事的电影。所以有一个叫做茱莉亚·罗伯茨的女人，她努力地去结婚却总是失败。

content.text: So it's called Run Away Bride. Because every time she goes to the altar, she gets nervous. She gets cold feet and she runs away.
content.trans: 所以它被称为“逃婚新娘”。因为每次她去教堂时，她都会紧张。她会退缩并跑开。

content.text: Alright, so they call her the Run Away Bride. I can't imagine this actually happening to someone. I mean, you have all your family there, your friends.
content.trans: 好的，所以她被称为逃婚新娘。我简直不敢相信这种事情真的会发生。我指的是你有你的家人和朋友。

content.text: You know, be so embarrassing. It's amazing. And expensive. Exactly. Because you've already paid for everything.
content.trans: 你知道，太丢人了。真神奇。又贵。因为你已经付过所有的钱了。

content.text: So do you get to eat the cake if you're the one who's left behind? I don't, I think so. Everything's paid for, right?
content.trans: 所以，如果你是最后一个留下来的人，你能吃到蛋糕吗？我觉得不是。一切都付了账。

content.text: Exactly. And drink all the liquor. Alright. So that's all the time we have for today. If you have any questions, any comments you can come to our website at EnglishPod.com. And we'll see you guys there.
content.trans: 的确。并且尽情饮酒吧。好的。今天的时间就到此为止了。如果你有任何问题或评论，欢迎访问我们的网站：EnglishPod.com，并与我们在这里会合。

content.text: Bye everyone. Bye.
content.trans: 再见大家。再见。

content.text: Bye.
content.trans: 再见。
